The agent should not generate copy from images alone when authoritative product facts are available elsewhere (content layer shown in the reference architecture).
Table header: Content Object | Purpose | Source / Rule

'Description' source/rule: Canonical facts.
'Description' source/rule: category context.
Content object 'Search keywords': purpose 'Search discoverability'.
'Search keywords' source/rule: Relevant terms grounded in product/category.
'Search keywords' source/rule: avoid unsupported claims.

'Backend/search fields' source/rule: Marketplace schema.

Golden Rule for AI Content (callout title)
Golden Rule: the agent may transform verified information.
Golden Rule: the agent may structure verified information.

Golden Rule: the agent must not invent measurements simply to complete a listing.

The canonical record becomes the source of truth before any marketplace-specific output is created.

### 11.1 Source-of-Truth Priority
Source-of-truth priority 1 (rendered '20.'): Seller-provided structured data.
Source-of-truth priority 2 (rendered '21.'): Seller-provided documents/labels/size charts.
Source-of-truth priority 2 (rendered '21.'): authoritative product assets.
Source-of-truth priority 3 (rendered '22.'): Connected catalog/PIM/ERP data.
Connected catalog/PIM/ERP data is used only if explicitly connected.
Connected catalog/PIM/ERP data is used only if trusted.
Source-of-truth priority 4 (rendered '23.'): Existing marketplace data.
Existing marketplace data is used only when it is the seller's own authoritative listing data.
Source-of-truth priority 5 (rendered '24.'): Derived values from deterministic normalization or category rules.
Source-of-truth priority 6 (rendered '25.'): AI-generated inference.
AI-generated inference only when the field is non-critical.
AI-generated inference only when the inference is clearly permitted.
Never use an AI guess to fill a critical factual/compliance field (rendered '26.').
## 12. Step-by-Step Autonomous Listing Workflow
Workflow STEP 1: UNDERSTAND PRODUCT.
Step 1 goal: build a complete understanding of the product before generating a marketplace listing.
Step 1 input: Seller form.
Step 1 input: Spreadsheet.
Step 1 input: Images.
Step 1 input: Website/catalog data.
Step 1 input: Size chart.
Step 1 input: Product documents.
Step 1 input: Connected systems.
Step 1 action: Identify product and variants.
Step 1 action: Separate facts from marketing language.
Step 1 action: Detect missing data.
Step 1 action: Detect conflicting data.
Step 1 action: Detect duplicate data.
Step 1 action: Determine reliable vs confirmation-needed facts.
Step 1 output: Structured product facts, each with source.
Step 1 output: Structured product facts, each with confidence.
Workflow STEP 2: CLASSIFY.
Step 2 goal: decide the correct product category and sub-category for each marketplace.
Step 2 action: Identify product type (T-shirt, shirt, dress, jeans, etc.).
Step 2 action: Identify audience/gender.
Step 2 action: Map canonical product to marketplace taxonomy.
Step 2 action: Verify seller category eligibility.
Step 2 action: Use evidence & rules (no random guesses).
Step 2 output: Canonical category.
Step 2 output: Marketplace-specific category/product type.
Step 2 output: Confidence.
Workflow STEP 3: EXTRACT ATTRIBUTES.
Step 3 goal: populate all product attributes from the available evidence.
Step 3 extract attribute: color
Step 3 extract attribute: size
Step 3 extract attribute: fabric
Step 3 extract attribute: fit
Step 3 extract attribute: pattern
Step 3 extract attribute: neckline
Step 3 extract attribute: sleeve
Step 3 extract attribute: length
Step 3 extract attribute: closure
Step 3 extract attribute: occasion
Step 3 action: Normalize synonyms into controlled values.
Step 3 action: Preserve original seller value.
Step 3 action: Preserve normalized value (alongside original seller value).
Step 3 action: Track source.
Step 3 action: Detect contradictions (e.g., '100% cotton' vs 'cotton-poly blend').
Step 3 output: Complete canonical attribute set.
Step 3 output: missing/conflicting fields identified.
Workflow STEP 4: FILL MARKETPLACE SCHEMA.
Step 4 goal: transform the canonical product into the exact field structure expected by each selected marketplace.
Step 4 action: Load current marketplace/category schema.
Step 4 action: Map canonical fields to portal fields.
Step 4 action: Apply allowed-value enums.
Step 4 action: Mark fields as required.
Step 4 action: Mark fields as conditional.
Step 4 action: Mark fields as optional.
Step 4 action: Mark fields as unsupported.
Step 4 action: Build parent/child variation structure.
Step 4 action: Map media roles.
Step 4 action: Map content fields.

Workflow STEP 5: GENERATE CONTENT.
Step 5 goal: create customer-facing listing content from verified product facts.
Step 5 creates: Title.
Step 5 creates: Bullets/key features.
Step 5 creates: Description.
Step 5 creates: Search keywords.
Step 5 creates: Size/fit copy.
Step 5 creates: Portal-specific content fields.
Step 5 rule: No unsupported claims.
Step 5 rule: No invented specs.
Step 5 rule: Do not copy prohibited content.
Step 5 rule: Keep consistent factual identity.
Step 5 rule: Adapt tone/format to marketplace rules.
Step 5 output: Content package with source traceability.
Workflow STEP 6: VALIDATE.
Step 6 goal: catch problems before marketplace submission.
Step 6 validate checklist: Required fields present.
Step 6 validate checklist: Allowed values.
Step 6 validate checklist: Parent/child relationship valid.
Step 6 validate checklist: Color consistency (color & size consistency).
Step 6 validate checklist: Size consistency (color & size consistency).
Step 6 validate checklist: Image presence.
Step 6 validate checklist: Image association.
Step 6 validate checklist: Price/MRP consistency.
Step 6 validate checklist: Product identifier rules.
Step 6 validate checklist: HSN/tax fields.
Step 6 validate checklist: Country of origin.
Step 6 validate checklist: Manufacturer details.
Step 6 validate checklist: Content policy checks.
Step 6 validate checklist: No conflicting facts.
Step 6 output value: `PASS`.
Step 6 output value: `BLOCKED`.
Step 6 output value: `NEEDS HUMAN INPUT`.
Step 6 output carries field-level reasons.
Workflow STEP 7: FIND MISSING DATA.
Step 7 goal: determine whether missing information can be recovered automatically.
Step 7: try missing-data sources in this strict hierarchy (order below).
Step 7 hierarchy 1: Existing canonical product record.
Step 7 hierarchy 2: Same brand's trusted catalog conventions.
Step 7 hierarchy 3: Connected PIM/ERP/catalog.
Step 7 hierarchy 4: Existing marketplace listing owned by the seller.
Step 7 hierarchy 5: Seller-provided files/assets.
Step 7 hierarchy 6: Deterministic category mapping.
Step 7 hierarchy 7: Ask seller.
Step 7 output: Missing fields reduced to the smallest set genuinely required.
Workflow STEP 8: ASK HUMAN ONLY WHEN NECESSARY.
Step 8 goal: ask the seller one clear question instead of sending them back to a large form.
Step 8 example question: 'What is the fabric composition: 100% cotton or 95% cotton / 5% elastane?'
Step 8 example question: 'Please provide the size chart for this product.'

Step 8 question must include: Optional safe suggestions.

Step 8 post-response: resume automatically from blocked step.
Workflow STEP 9: SUBMIT.

Step 11 goal: diagnose and resolve errors without making the seller repeat the process.
Step 11, for every error: Capture error code/message.
Step 11, for every error: Identify affected SKU/field.
Step 11, for every error: Translate to plain language.
Step 11, for every error: Determine if auto-fixable.
Step 11, for every error: Apply deterministic fix.
Step 11, for every error: Revalidate.
Step 11 auto-fixable class: Wrong portal enum mapped from known canonical value.

Step 11 human-required class: Conflicting seller data.
Step 11 human-required class: Brand authorization/approval.
Step 11 human-required class: Account issue.
Step 11 human-required class: Compliance evidence request.

Step 12 goal: send the corrected listing back to the marketplace.
Step 12 action: Keep same seller SKU/identity.

Step 12 action: Submit only after validation passes.

Workflow STEP 13: CONFIRM LIVE.
Step 13 goal: confirm the product is genuinely sellable/live.

Step 13 minimum confirmation: Marketplace ID captured.
Step 13 minimum confirmation: Seller SKU mapped.

Workflow STEP 14: SHOW DASHBOARD STATUS.
Step 14 goal: give the seller a simple operational view.
Step 14 show: Overall status.
Step 14 show: Per-marketplace status.
Step 14 show: Current step.
Step 14 show: Issue count.
Step 14 show: Human actions required.
Step 14 show: Last sync.
Step 14 show: Marketplace listing ID/SKU.
Step 14 show: Live URL.
Step 14 show: Attempt history.

## 13. Listing Status Model
The product tracks granular operational status across all lifecycle phases.
Table header: Status | Meaning | Seller Action
Listing status `DRAFT`: Product information has been started but is not ready.
Seller action for `DRAFT`: Provide missing information if shown.
Listing status `UNDERSTANDING`: Agent is interpreting product inputs.
Seller action for `UNDERSTANDING`: None
Listing status `CLASSIFYING`: Agent is selecting category/product type.
Seller action for `CLASSIFYING`: None unless ambiguous.
Listing status `READY_FOR_REVIEW`: Draft is structurally ready but requires seller confirmation.
Seller action for `READY_FOR_REVIEW`: Review only if requested by workflow.
Listing status `READY_TO_LIST`: Validation passed for selected marketplace(s).
Seller action for `READY_TO_LIST`: None
Listing status `SUBMITTING`: Listing is being sent.
Seller action for `SUBMITTING`: None
Listing status `PROCESSING`: Marketplace is processing the submission.
Seller action for `PROCESSING`: None
Listing status `LIVE`: Marketplace confirmed the listing is active/live.
Seller action for `LIVE`: None
Listing status `PARTIALLY_LIVE`: Some variants/marketplaces are live while others are not.
Seller action for `PARTIALLY_LIVE`: Resolve failed portions if needed.
Listing status `BLOCKED`: Required information/permission/compliance issue prevents progress.
Seller action for `BLOCKED`: Complete the displayed task.
Listing status `ERROR`: Submission/validation failed.
Seller action for `ERROR`: Usually none if auto-fix is possible.
Seller action for `ERROR`: otherwise resolve task.
Listing status `HUMAN_ACTION_REQUIRED`: Agent cannot safely proceed without seller input/action.
Seller action for `HUMAN_ACTION_REQUIRED`: Answer the exact question or perform the requested marketplace action.
Listing status `PAUSED`: Seller or system intentionally paused the listing.
Seller action for `PAUSED`: Resume when ready.
Listing status `ARCHIVED`: Listing workflow is closed.
Seller action for `ARCHIVED`: None

## 15. Error Management Framework
Table header: Error Class | Example | Agent Behavior
Error class 'Missing data' (example: Fabric composition absent).
Agent behavior for 'Missing data': Find source.
Agent behavior for 'Missing data': if source unavailable, ask seller.
Error class 'Invalid value' (example: Marketplace does not accept seller's color term).
Agent behavior for 'Invalid value': Map to allowed marketplace value.
Error class 'Category mismatch' (example: Product mapped to wrong product type).
Agent behavior for 'Category mismatch': Reclassify.
Agent behavior for 'Category mismatch': Remap.
Error class 'Variation error' (example: Size/color relationship invalid).
Agent behavior for 'Variation error': Rebuild mapping from canonical variant matrix.
Error class 'Media error' (example: Image not accepted).
Agent behavior for 'Media error': Identify failed image rule.
Agent behavior for 'Media error': Replace/remap if possible.
Error class 'Content error' (example: Title/field violates marketplace rule).
Agent behavior for 'Content error': Rewrite using verified facts.
Error class 'Identifier error' (example: GTIN/identifier issue).
Agent behavior for 'Identifier error': Ask seller.
Agent behavior for 'Identifier error': Use approved exemption flow if applicable.
Error class 'Compliance error' (example: Required declaration missing).
Agent behavior for 'Compliance error': Request exact compliance information.
Error class 'Account permission' (example: Seller not approved for category/brand).
Agent behavior for 'Account permission': Create human action task.
Error class 'Marketplace outage/technical' (example: Submission unavailable).
Agent behavior for 'Marketplace outage/technical': Retry according to safe retry policy.
Agent behavior for 'Marketplace outage/technical': Do not create duplicates.

Important Anti-Loop Rule (callout title)
The agent must never repeatedly submit the same failed listing indefinitely.
Every retry needs a changed input, a known retryable condition, or a marketplace status transition that justifies another attempt.
## 16. Human-in-the-Loop Rules
The product should be autonomous by default.
The product should not be reckless (autonomous by default, but not reckless).
Human involvement is a controlled exception.
Table header: Ask the Seller When | Do NOT Ask When
Ask the seller when: A critical factual field is genuinely missing.
Do NOT ask the seller when: The answer already exists in the canonical record.
Ask the seller when: Two authoritative sources conflict.
Do NOT ask the seller when: The value can be deterministically normalized.
Ask the seller when: Marketplace requires seller-specific approval/evidence.
Do NOT ask the seller when: The agent can safely transform an existing value.
Ask the seller when: A compliance declaration cannot be verified.
Do NOT ask the seller when: The missing value is merely a formatting variation.
Ask the seller when: A category/brand permission decision is required.
Do NOT ask the seller when: The marketplace has a known mapping for the category.
